_1_what_this_is: The two Draw Things configs, and the two canvas sizes, held outside build_project.py so
swapping models never means editing the generator. build_project.py copies each object in
'configShortcuts' verbatim into the emitted project's own configShortcuts map, and the two
phase 'config' items reference them by name (#krea2_stills / #ltx2_video).
Shortcuts are an Editor-format concept. Both exporters resolve them before the pipeline ever
toPipelineArray config branch), so the running pipeline gets a plain inline config object.
_2_todo_ned: Every value below that reads exactly "TODO_NED" is a placeholder and the project will NOT
render correctly until it is replaced. verify_project.py lists them all; run it with --strict
to turn that list into a hard failure before a real run.
These values are deliberately NOT guessed. Sampler and seedMode are integer enums whose
meaning changes between Draw Things builds, model filenames are exact strings including the
quantisation suffix, and the tiling fields only matter at particular canvas sizes. A
plausible-looking wrong value is worse than an obvious placeholder: it runs, and it runs wrong.
_3_where_the_values_come_from: 1. In Draw Things, render ONE still with the Krea 2 model at the phase-A canvas size.
2. Render ONE clip with LTX-2 at the phase-B canvas size.
3. In Tanque Studio: Import from DT, select each render, and read its config off the
Metadata (raw) viewer. That is the authoritative copy — it is what DT actually used,
not what a UI panel was displaying.
4. Paste the integer/string values into the matching keys below. Keep the key names.
complete Krea 2 Turbo config from the format's author. It is the shape to match — but its
values are for a 1920x1280 canvas, so its tiling fields do not transfer unchanged.
_4_quotes: TODO_NED is quoted only because a placeholder has to be SOME valid JSON. When you replace
it, use the field's real type. 'model' is the only one of the 22 that stays a quoted string.
WHY IT MATTERS: the pipeline applies a config with Object.assign(configuration, value)
(StoryflowPipeline.js:1002) and coerces nothing. "seedMode": "2" hands Draw Things the
STRING "2" for an integer enum — valid JSON, exports fine, wrong at the far end. This is
unlike 'sweep', whose numeric-looking cards ARE coerced to real numbers on export, so the
habit does not transfer. verify_project.py fails on any quoted number or boolean here.
The author's own config in misc/.../CharacterSheet_3x2_1920x1280.json is the reference:
every numeric field in it is bare.

_5_key_notes.model: Exact checkpoint filename including extension, e.g. 'krea_2_turbo_q8p.ckpt'.
_5_key_notes.sampler: INTEGER enum, not a name and not a quoted digit. Read it off a real render.
_5_key_notes.seedMode: INTEGER enum, not a name and not a quoted digit. Read it off a real render.
_5_key_notes.numFrames: Phase A pins 1 deliberately (plan 5.2): 'configuration' persists across the whole run, so on a second pass phase B's framesDialog would otherwise leave it high and Krea 2 would be asked for a video. Do not remove it.
_5_key_notes.seed: Phase A ships -1 because the phase-A 'sweep' item overrides it per character from bible.json's seed column. Phase B stays -1 on purpose: seed does not carry identity into an image-to-video pass, the anchor does.
_5_key_notes.tiledDecoding + decodingTile*: Only meaningful past roughly one megapixel. Whether you need them depends on the canvas size in 'sizes' below and on your machine.
_5_key_notes.loras: Empty list ships. A camera-control / static-shot LoRA on the LTX-2 config is worth trying, since the whole shot design is 'the camera does not move'. Shape: [{"file": "...", "mode": "all", "weight": 1.0}].

_6_sizes_and_pacing: 'sizes' feeds the two 'size' items, one per phase. Keep every dimension divisible by 32.
OPEN QUESTION, worth settling BEFORE writing the bible: the shipped stills are square and the
shipped video is 16:9. Phase A's output is phase B's first frame, so a square anchor gets
reframed on the way into the clip. Matching the aspect (e.g. stills at 1024x576 too) avoids
that. Changing it later means regenerating every anchor.
'framesDialog' is the clip-length rule. padding is 48, NOT the Editor's default of 49:
framesDialog() returns ceil(words/wps*25 / 8)*8 + 1 and the executor then adds padding raw
(StoryflowPipeline.js:1045), so 8k+1+49 = 8k+50, which is 2 mod 8 and not a valid LTX frame
count. 48 gives 8k+49, which is 1 mod 8. Costs 0.04s of tail.
WARNING: the StoryFlow Editor's own padding field will silently snap 48 back to 49. Its
clampPadding (StoryflowEditor.html:~1455) rounds to the nearest 8k+1. If you open this
project in the Editor and touch the framesDialog item, re-run build_project.py afterwards.
